title: Projectome hierarchy did not predict a reliable map of intrinsic activity timescales across 65 regions of the larval zebrafish brain (22 fish, mapZebrain trophic levels)
abstract: Question: in primate cortex, areas higher in the anatomical hierarchy have longer intrinsic timescales. Earlier campaign work found no reliable relation in mouse cortex and an opposite relation in moving C. elegans. We tested the rule in the larval zebrafish. Data: whole-brain two-photon calcium imaging of 22 larvae (Legare et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0; about 1.23 million neurons; 570 s of spontaneous activity at about 1 volume/s) and the authors' directed mapZebrain projectome (70 regions). Method (pre-specified): per-neuron autocorrelation after removal of a swim-locked response; per fish and region, an exponential fit on lags 1-30 s; region value = median over fish. The primary structure measure was the trophic level of each region. P-values came from 1,000 spatially autocorrelated surrogate maps. Results: region timescales ranged from 3.9 to 38.5 s (median 9.0 s) and were reliable between halves of the fish (split-half rho 0.83). Trophic level did not predict timescale (65 regions; rho -0.045; spatial-null p 0.77; fish-bootstrap 95% interval -0.15 to +0.03; partial rho after five nuisance controls -0.01). Eight other projectome measures, including hop distance from sensory ganglia and in-strength, also gave no spatial-null p below 0.05 (1 of 54 estimator-measure tests did). A weak negative value for one trophic variant came only from six peripheral sensory organs and ganglia, which had about twofold longer population timescales (exploratory). Limitations: the projectome is sparse, dense and weakly hierarchical (trophic incoherence 0.84); the slow nuclear indicator limits timescales to seconds; connectome and activity come from different animals.

display.caption: Region log10 timescale (median over 22 fish) against projectome trophic level (primary), SC in-strength and the first SC gradient. Values above each panel: Spearman rho, p from 1,000 spatially autocorrelated surrogates, and partial rho after five nuisance controls. Orange diamonds: peripheral sensory organs and ganglia.

A: mean neuron autocorrelation and exponential fits for three regions. B: region timescales at atlas centroids (dorsal view). C: split-half reliability of six timescale estimators over random halves of the fish. D: timescale of all 65 regions, median and interquartile range over fish.
A: Spearman rho between region timescale and nine structural measures for six timescale estimators (* spatial-null p < 0.05; 1 of 54). B: per-fish rho for the primary estimator.
